tone_statements.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2006. La participation des consonnes comme unités porteuses de ton en kotafon, dialecte gbe du Sud-Bénin. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 87-107.
tone_statements.quote: Alors que le ton B des radicaux verbaux correspond toujours au ton B dans les autres dialectes gbe, le ton BH correspond aux tons H, BH et M des autres dialectes gbe, comme nous le montrent les tableaux suivants: Tableau 3: Correspondance BH = M au niveau des radicaux verbaux CcV, dont C = [+obstr., +voix] [columns: Kotafon | Xwla-sɛmɛ | ... | Xwla | Xwela | Gloses]
tone_statements.translation: Whereas the L tone of verb radicals always corresponds to L tone in the other Gbe dialects, the LH tone corresponds to the tones H, LH and M of the other Gbe dialects, as the following tables show: Table 3: Correspondence LH = M in CV verb radicals whose C is [+obstruent, +voice] [columns: Kotafon | Xwla-Sèmè | ... | Xwla | Xwela | glosses]
tone_statements.locator: p. 92, sec. 3.3 'La distribution du ton BH', Table 3 (same passage in Gbéto 2004 SAL 33(1) p. 73, sec. 4.3)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

sources.citation: Henson, Bonnie J. & Angela Kluge. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 5: Xwla language area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-017. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (word lists, RA-RTT comprehension, vitality). Sec. 3 'Previous linguistic research' (pp. 5-7) names only Capo 1986/1991 (comparative Gbe phonology; Xwla = Capo's 'Phla') and SIL/CNL word lists as prior work. 'accent' only in the folk sense: sec. 6.1 p. 11 'no dialects of Xwla, though there are distinguishable accents from one village to another'; sec. 6.1.3 contact 'begins to impact the Xwla tones, accents and even words'. Covers western (Togo/Grand-Popo) and eastern (Ouémé) Xwla.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo: Gbe language family overview. SIL ESR 2011-012. 21 pp; and Kluge, Angela. 2008. The Gbe language varieties of West Africa: a quantitative analysis of lexical and grammatical features. SIL ESR 2008-023. 214 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Classification/lexicostatistics; Xwla split into western (Adamé) and eastern (Djeffa, 'Movolo' per Capo 1999) varieties; word lists entered without tone. Cites Henson & Kluge 1999 unpublished Xwla survey (= 2011 ESR 2011-017).

sources.citation: PHOIBLE inventory GM 1280 'western xwla' (source: Capo 1991). Moran & McCloy (eds.) 2019, PHOIBLE 2.0.
sources.note: Segment inventory only; tones listed ˦ (H), ˨ (L), ˦˨ (HL). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2006. La participation des consonnes comme unités porteuses de ton en kotafon, dialecte gbe du Sud-Bénin. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 87-107.
sources.quote: Alors que le ton B des radicaux verbaux correspond toujours au ton B dans les autres dialectes gbe, le ton BH correspond aux tons H, BH et M des autres dialectes gbe, comme nous le montrent les tableaux suivants: Tableau 3: Correspondance BH = M au niveau des radicaux verbaux CcV, dont C = [+obstr., +voix] [columns: Kotafon | Xwla-sɛmɛ | ... | Xwla | Xwela | Gloses]
sources.locator: p. 92, sec. 3.3 'La distribution du ton BH', Table 3 (same passage in Gbéto 2004 SAL 33(1) p. 73, sec. 4.3)
sources.note: Kotafon has two underlying tones H and L with M, LH, HL, MH, HM derived and voiceless obstruents inserting H; for Xwla the paper gives only comparative verb-root data (sec. 3.3, p. 92, Tables 3-4): Kotafon LH on voiced-obstruent-initial CV verb radicals corresponds to M in Xwla and Xwla-sɛmɛ (ji 'gonfle!', vi 'pleure!', dɔ 'dors!'), and L corresponds to L across all Gbe dialects. Confirms lexical tone with L/M/H surface levels on Xwla verb roots; no Xwla-internal analysis.

sources.citation: Hounzangbe, Zinsou & Maxime da Cruz. 2023. La designation des concepts colere et patience dans les langues du continuum dialectal Gbe, cas du xwlagbe. Akofena n008, vol. 2: 175-192. doi 10.48734/akofena.n008v02.15.2023.
sources.note: No tone section: a lexical-semantic/morphosyntagmatic study of 'anger' and 'patience' expressions. Data are tone-marked with acute/grave diacritics (e.g. vivé, ɔdɔmɛ̀) and one passing first-hand remark says the verb vɛ 'porte un ton moyen contrairement aux cas precedents' (p. 182 area, ex. 7), i.e. the authors operate with high, low and mid tones in Grand-Popo Xwla; no inventory, TBU or sandhi statement.
